notes: T662 (the token split and the pi-session meter) — item #0 of the measurement programme, measurement-methodology.md §6 (a)+(b); Fable's retirement sweep. THE GAP, CONFIRMED: (1) claude lanes report a total that is 99.9% cache — T620's run record is tokens_in=1,386,293 of which tokens_fresh=1,603 and tokens_cache_read=1,384,690 — so charging a lane for 1.39M input when it consumed 1.6k fresh is off by three orders of magnitude; (2) pi lanes report NOTHING — every deepseek/ollama record carries 'tokens: no reading — no structured usage in process output (pi/ollama lane); raw stdout+stderr teed to untracked/tokens/; the pi session JSONL is the retroactive meter' and session 'no handle — ... the session id is not emitted at dispatch' (quoted RED from the live ledger: T650/T660/T661 rows), and NOTHING read that meter. (a) THE PI-SESSION METER IS NOW READ INTO THE LANE RECORDS: bin/subagent passes `--session untracked/tokens/sessions/<task>.<epoch>.jsonl` to the deepseek pi lane and to the INNER pi of the ollama lane (`ollama launch pi --model <tag> -y -- --session <path> -p ...`); the path is unique per dispatch attempt (the T650 principle — a re-dispatch never overwrites a previous attempt's session). The runner mkdirs the session parent at launch (pi does not), and after the child closes reads the JSONL via the new tc.read_pi_session(): tokens_in = input + cacheRead, tokens_fresh = input, tokens_cache_read = cacheRead, tokens_out = output, source=pi-session-jsonl, session_id (the JSONL session header's id — the resumable handle) and session_path, stamped on all three surfaces (run record untracked/runs/<task>.json, the [runner] trailer line, the ledger untracked/tokens/tokens.jsonl). THE KNOWN GAP ('session id is not emitted at dispatch') IS SOLVED by passing the session PATH at dispatch — pi writes to exactly that file, so the meter has a known per-lane file; the id is recovered from the file at close and recorded. FALLBACK, stated precisely: a pi/ollama lane WITHOUT --session (a hand-run command, a legacy launcher) records UNKNOWN with the exact reason — the default dir ~/.pi/agent/sessions/<cwd-slug>/ holds concurrent lanes' files and the uuid is not attributable, so scanning it would guess; the cost of the fallback is that the lane's reading is lost (never 0, never the total). ROBUSTNESS GUARD: the runner calls read_pi_session via getattr, so a tree whose token-capture.py is an OLDER copy degrades to UNKNOWN-with-reason, never a crash (the 2026-08-22 acd7451 worktree incident — HEAD runner calling read_pi_session against a HEAD token-capture.py lacking it — is exactly that shape; it broke the bakeoff-gates worktree arm for the ~3 minutes the pair was half-committed, and the guard makes it structurally impossible again). (b) THE SPLIT: tokens_in keeps its meaning (input + cache_read) and tokens_fresh / tokens_cache_read ride beside it on EVERY family's records, stamped ALWAYS (nulls included). claude: real split from the T521 envelope (fresh=input, cache_read=cache_read) — already landed by T558; this row re-pins the sum invariant (regression arm B: 44 = 11 + 33; the real T620 record: 1,386,293 = 1,603 + 1,384,690). pi/ollama: real split from the session JSONL usage object, which carries input and cacheRead separately for BOTH deepseek and local ollama (the same usage shape observed in real session files of both providers). UNKNOWN — never 0, never the total — for: a lane whose session file is MISSING after close (recorded loudly: 'pi session JSONL unreadable: session file missing: <path>', all three token fields None), a lane without --session, and a tree lacking the reader. A silent zero here would be a free lane in the cost ladder. D044 (2026-08-22, directive from T612, ACKED AND ACTED ON): every token record must carry its timestamp (already present — run record start/start_epoch, ledger ts) and the resolved deepseek peak/off-peak band computed at write time (measurement-methodology.md §1b): new rate_band field on the run record + ledger — 'peak' (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC weekdays) / 'off-peak' (all else incl. the UTC Fri 16:00 -> Sun 16:00 weekend override) for deepseek lanes, null + a family-naming reason for others (claude: anthropic team subscription — occupancy of the five-hour rolling window, no per-token price; ollama: credits, no peak concept; other: no time-priced rate). Band boundaries unit-tested (Tue 02:00 peak; Tue 05:00 off-peak; Fri 17:00 override off-peak; Sun 07:00 — a peak HOUR overridden to off-peak; Mon 02:00 peak after the override; unparseable -> None). WHAT AN ECONOMY FIGURE MAY AND MAY NOT BE COMPUTED FROM (ruling 35 + §1b + D044): MAY — within a family, from records whose split is REAL (source claude-json-envelope or pi-session-jsonl, tokens_fresh and tokens_cache_read both numeric) and whose run is not censored (killed_by = none, ruling 32). MAY NOT — cross-family economy as one number: the families are NOT in the same units (claude = subscription/occupancy of the five-hour rolling window, a lane costs what it displaces; deepseek = per-token at a clock-varying rate; ollama = credits; local = the machine), so 'verified findings / output tokens' is meaningful within a family and a category error across one; a cross-family cost claim must state its unit and defend it, and NO conversion factor between a subscription and a per-token rate is invented here. NEVER — from a record whose split is UNKNOWN (tokens_fresh/tokens_cache_read None): a silent zero becomes a free lane. And a budget meter must read tokens_fresh, never tokens_in — tokens_in counts cache reads as consumption (D043's exact inflation: T620's 1.39M 'in' is 99.9% cache; the split this row lands is what makes a correct meter possible).
